FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 236
Committee: State Governmental Affairs Sponsor: Senator Larry Stutts
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/02/2024
Senate Bill 236 as introduced would decrease certificate of need receipts to the State Health
Planning and Development Agency (SHPDA) by an undetermined amount dependent on the
number of rural health care providers located outside of a metropolitan statistical area, pursuant
to the provisions of this bill, beginning October 1, 2024 that would no longer need a certificate
of need (CON) to: (1) propose, acquire, construct, operate, furnish or offer a new institutional
health service; or (2) arrange or commit to the financing of a new institutional health service.
According to SHPDA, the average annual application fees collected from facilities classified as
rural was $53,000 based on fiscal year 2022 and fiscal year 2023 data.
